newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: OPEC possible target of Vienna hotel bugging.
newsitem.headline: OPEC possible target of Vienna hotel bugging.

text.p: Austria said on Monday it believed foreign secret agents had bugged a top Vienna hotel in what one report alleged was a CIA operation to eavesdrop on Iraqi and Iranian OPEC delegates.
"Bugging devices were found in the (Marriott) hotel....and we're now investigating in all directions," Interior Ministry spokesman Rudolf Gollia told Reuters.
"Signs point towards a foreign organisation, presumably a foreign secret service."
Decorators found bugging devices in the walls at the Marriott hotel on Vienna's imperial Ringstrasse during renovation six weeks ago, general manager Stefan Kocsi said.
The plush hotel has long been favoured by oil ministers and delegates of the 12-nation Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries. OPEC is based in Vienna and ministers meet there twice a year.

Weekly current affairs magazine Profil said in a report published on Monday that Germany's secret service tipped off its Austrian counterpart that the U.S. Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) eavesdropped on Iranian and Iraqi delegates during an OPEC meeting last November.
The motive was a dispute over raising oil export quotas in southern Iraq, Profil said.

The United Nations gave Iraq clearance in December for limited exports under an oil-for-food deal so it could import relief aid for its 20 million citizens, living under U.N. trade sanctions imposed since Iraq invaded Kuwait in August 1990.
The deal, which expires in June, meant Iraq could export oil for the first time since the Gulf War.
A spokeswoman for the U.S. embassy in Vienna said the United States had no information on the hotel bugging.
"In any event, we have no comment on intelligence issues," she said.
An OPEC spokesman said he was unable to comment on the bugging. "We've just heard about it ourselves this morning," he said.
Marriott general manager Kocsi said bugging devices had been found in three rooms but it was impossible to say how long they had been installed and at whom they were targeted.
"Many famous people stay at our hotel but we don't have a clue as to who the target was. It's just speculation," he said.
The Interior Ministry's Gollia said the authorities would not be conducting a search of other Vienna hotels, but added that some managers of hotels used by OPEC may be inclined to do so themselves.
The Hilton hotel said it would conduct a thorough inspection of its hotel rooms for bugs, while the ANA Grand and Intercontinental said a search was unnecessary.
The bugging revelations are an embarrassment to Austria, which prides itself on Vienna's reputation as host to international organisations.
